# ferriskey_client_scope_assignment (Resource)

Attaches a client scope to a client as a `default` or `optional` scope. The assignment is a pure link: any change forces it to be recreated. New clients are automatically given the realm's default scopes, so assigning one of those fails because it is already attached.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ferriskey_client_scope_assignment" "billing" {
  realm     = ferriskey_realm.acme.name
  client_id = ferriskey_client.web.client_uuid
  scope_id  = ferriskey_client_scope.billing.scope_id
  type      = "optional"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) UUID of the client. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `realm` (String) Realm the client and scope belong to. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `scope_id` (String) UUID of the client scope. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `type` (String) Assignment type: `default` or `optional`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite identifier `{realm}/{client_id}/{scope_id}`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ferriskey_client_scope_assignment.billing acme/7f3a9b10-1111-2222-3333-444455556666/4b2d7f90-1111-2222-3333-444455556666
```
